clue.text: Channel taking middle course

explanation.surface: A broadcaster or waterway steering a moderate path.
explanation.definitionFit: A medium is a channel of communication, and a happy medium is a compromise between extremes.

clue.text: In Paris he could create some ruin!

indicators.note: creating something new from these words means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Someone in the French capital might wreak a bit of havoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could create' rearranges SOME RUIN. 'In Paris he' is the definition: the French title for a man, used as we use 'Mr' or 'sir'.
explanation.definitionFit: The French form of address for a gentleman, the equivalent of Mister.

clue.text: Friar may have same small car first

indicators.note: first puts the same and the small car ahead of the remaining piece

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same
the Mini is a classic small British car
may, in the sense of being able or allowed, is can

explanation.surface: A monk might own an identical little car before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' says the ditto and the car come before the final piece; 'have' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dominican is a member of the order of preaching friars founded by St Dominic.

clue.text: Unvarying outfit

explanation.surface: Clothing that never changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform means constant, and it is also the standard dress worn by members of a group.

clue.text: Hung on, finished after a very gentle start

indicators.note: after puts the word for finished behind the very gentle start

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very soft playing
finished means ended

explanation.surface: Someone held on and completed a task after starting softly.
explanation.walkthrough: PP is pianissimo, a musical instruction to play very quietly; 'start' is a link saying A and PP come first.
explanation.definitionFit: Something appended is attached or tacked onto the end, hung on to something else.

clue.text: Mad prince's advance closing in on enemy?

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters of the royal word are crazily jumbled

parts.note: the royal's letters taken as written, the possessive adding none
an advance by troops is a movement

explanation.surface: A crazed royal marches forward on a hostile force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges PRINCE to give PINCER.
explanation.definitionFit: A military tactic in which two forces converge from both flanks to surround a foe.

clue.text: Fast train say

explanation.surface: A remark about a quick railway service.
explanation.definitionFit: An express is a train making few stops, and to express something is to put it into words.

clue.text: Clever to hide £1 inside pottery

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it within, so the pound sign goes in the middle

parts.note: clever means deft
L stands for libra, the pound

explanation.surface: A smart person conceals a pound note inside some crockery.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra; 'inside' just repeats the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Delft is the blue-and-white tin-glazed earthenware named after a Dutch town.

clue.text: Wish of father across the channel

parts.note: across the channel, in French, of is de
a sire is a father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A dad's longing from somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across the channel' tells you 'of' is translated into French, giving DE.
explanation.definitionFit: Desire is a strong longing or want, as a wish is.

clue.text: Manufacture on a large scale in a service industry?

explanation.surface: Industrial output in a business that serves customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading treats Mass as a church service, so its staging is a 'production'.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory output in huge volume; whimsically, putting on a church Mass is making a service.

clue.text: In the main imbibing contents of clouds

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Out at sea, someone is drinking in what the sky holds.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across maIN IMBIbing; 'the' and 'contents of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Nimbi is the plural of nimbus, a rain-bearing cloud.

clue.text: New pianolas about halfway through month coming from us city

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around another piece
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of pianolas
halfway through a five-letter word is its third, central letter

explanation.surface: Fresh player pianos arrive from America mid-month.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of PIANOLAS goes 'about' N, the middle letter of MONTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Annapolis is the state capital of Maryland, home of the US Naval Academy.

clue.text: Go in with sue smashing type of rock

indicators.note: smashing breaks the letters apart so they can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Enter and take legal action, breaking up a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' rearranges GO IN and SUE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous rock forms from cooled magma or lava, like granite or basalt.

clue.text: Choose gold constituent

parts.note: to choose by vote is to elect
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Select a golden ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; 'constituent' means a voter in a constituency, not an ingredient.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituent is a voter represented by a member of parliament.

clue.text: A French commander with rosy was out-and-out

parts.note: the French for a is un
Com is an abbreviation for commander
a rosy outlook is a promising one

explanation.surface: A French officer with a hopeful outlook was thorough.
explanation.walkthrough: COM is a dictionary abbreviation for commander; 'with' and 'was' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something total and unyielding, with no concessions made.

clue.text: Stole old hat and left in a hurry

parts.note: to nip is slang for to steal, so stole is nipped
old hat means out of fashion, out

explanation.surface: A thief pinched an old hat and dashed off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stole' is the verb, not a scarf, and 'old hat' is the phrase meaning unfashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: To nip out is to pop out quickly, departing briefly in haste.

clue.text: Get a word in here towards the side

explanation.surface: Squeezing a comment in from the sidelines.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition completes the idiom 'get a word in edgeways', said when someone talks nonstop.
explanation.definitionFit: Completes the idiom about barely managing to speak, and means sideways, with the edge foremost.

clue.text: Not above having grown without means for economic growth

parts.note: not above means below, under
having grown means developed

explanation.surface: Something below after growing up, yet lacking the means to prosper.
explanation.definitionFit: An underdeveloped country lacks the industry and infrastructure for a strong economy.

clue.text: Wild ragweed on the road in London

indicators.note: wild suggests the weed's letters are running riot

explanation.surface: Uncultivated weeds grow by a road in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges RAGWEED. Edgware is a district of north London, and Edgware Road is a well-known London street.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgware Road is a major London thoroughfare, so this name stands on that road.

clue.text: The devil of a match

explanation.surface: A fiendish contest.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucifer is a name for Satan, and an old word for a friction match.

clue.text: Little creature reportedly caught sight of cockney lady

indicators.note: reportedly means we hear the phrase spoken rather than written

parts.note: caught sight of means spied; a cockney drops the h of her, saying 'er

explanation.surface: A small animal seemingly glimpsed a woman from East London.
explanation.walkthrough: A cockney, a Londoner from the East End, drops initial H, so 'spied her' sounds like the creature.
explanation.definitionFit: A small eight-legged arachnid is a little creature.

clue.text: Force other plaice to go round inhabiting the sea

indicators.note: to go round means the rearranged fish encircles another letter
other means the letters of the fish are made different

parts.note: G is the symbol for gravitational force

explanation.surface: A fish is made to circle in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges PLAICE and that anagram goes 'round' G.
explanation.definitionFit: Pelagic describes creatures living in the open ocean rather than near shore or seabed.

clue.text: Ring up about single shrub

indicators.note: about means the reversed word wraps around the one
in a down clue, up means the word for ring reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone
single is one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Phone round about a lone bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns CALL into LLAC, which goes 'about' I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blooms.

clue.text: Knife used by Scotsman, the man taking note

parts.note: Mac is a familiar address for a Scotsman
the man is he
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A Scot wields a blade while a fellow plays music.
explanation.walkthrough: TE is a note in the do-re-mi scale; 'used by' and 'taking' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A machete is a broad heavy blade used for cutting vegetation.

clue.text: Croatian dog?

parts.note: a breed of hound named after a region on the Adriatic coast of Croatia

explanation.surface: Is this hound from the Balkans?
explanation.walkthrough: The spotted breed takes its name from Dalmatia, the Croatian coastal region, so the question mark flags a literal reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted breed shares its name with an inhabitant of Dalmatia in Croatia.

clue.text: State I'd removed plants

indicators.note: removed means the letters of I'd are taken out

parts.note: Florida is a US state
I'd gives the letters ID, the apostrophe adding none

explanation.surface: A government said it had cleared out vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ID out of FLORIDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Flora is the plant life of a region, collectively.

clue.text: Cowardly carpenter in trouble quietly leaves

indicators.note: in trouble suggests the letters are thrown into disorder
leaves means the quiet letter departs from the word

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical marking for quietly

explanation.surface: A timid woodworker in difficulty slips away silently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quietly leaves' takes P out of CARPENTER, and 'in trouble' rearranges the remaining CARENTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Recreant is an old word for craven, faint-hearted or disloyal.

clue.text: Soldiers caught blackleg for nothing

indicators.note: caught means the soldiers hold the traitor inside

parts.note: GIs are American soldiers
a blackleg, a strikebreaker, is a rat

explanation.surface: Troops captured a strikebreaker with nothing to show for it.
explanation.walkthrough: A blackleg is British slang for someone who keeps working during a strike, scorned as a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratis means free of charge, at no cost.
